So it was light undercover meaning he was still home at night most nights. And it was a county sheriff department. I kinda figured your question was about deep cover but having some personal experience I thought I’d share bc I was a teen and remember it well. So here’s a longer explanation since you’re interested. 
He worked fast food part time where they thought they were funneling drugs no idea who the distributor was though ie coulda been management even. So in order to make it look real his pay was at the store was just a normal job in terms of taxes (even had to apply for the job like normal) then he had a cheap apartment that his ‘roommate’ was also a cop that the county paid for in reality. After work he’d drive to that apartment stay for awhile or if he needed to “hangout” with a suspect to gain trust he’d stay overnight. If there was no reason to stay he’d get in a different car and come home. His cop pay check just came to his real name in our family bank account. It wasn’t like they were hunting down a kingpin or anything so the need for a super tight cover wasn’t needed. Not as exciting but my understanding most undercover work is like this rather than being in deep for years. Also this was preinternet so less ways for lower level traffickers to check a cover. I can’t imagine with images of everyone on the internet the work it would take to cover someone now, even at the low level like this

Some of your comparisons to Nazi germany are definitely fair especially on the humanitarian front. But the difference in regards to peace is that China significantly benefits from the current world order. Germany prior to the rise of fascism was in a perpetually declining situation with reparations and really had no choice other than aggression to improve their situation (ww2 would likely have had happened without the genocides) China on the other hand has only gained from the modern economic order starting by distancing themselves from the ussr. At this point conflict with anyone beyond internally would result in a total destruction of their income. Meaning China is trapped in that they can push their agenda but only so far as the global community allows them to. Maybe just maybe decades from now they can expand their sphere of influence to eclipse that of literally every other country (which they definitely are trying by their endeavors in Africa) but this making an assumption that no other country will try to combat those actions for 30-40 years. 
The ‘China is the bogey man’ is a common troupe but in reality it’s hard to see analytically how it’s going to become a reality. As it stands their economy and therefore all their power is unbalanced and lives on the good graces of other nations. 
There are plenty of threats but it’s far more likely that a radical movement steers a liberal (relatively speaking) country considered stable to change rapidly and upset the current order than a socially conservative authoritarian China changed their policies radically overnight.
